findings.description: During the first airborne trick the board's underside (trucks facing camera) is solid black at 1.75-2.25s, abruptly becomes light beige/wood-coloured at 2.5s, then dark/teal again at 2.75s. The same board's underside is light grey in the second trick (8.0-8.5s), so the black bottom at 2.0-2.25s is inconsistent with the board's identity; no lighting change explains the flip.

Skater and board stay airborne from about 1.5s to 3.25s (~1.75s) on near-flat ground, hovering at a constant height with no slow-motion cues (camera moves at normal speed). Real airtime for this kind of flatground flip is roughly 0.5s, so the hang time looks implausible.

At the first landing the board is smeared and partially missing: its deck dissolves under the feet, one wheel shows below the front shoe, and the feet don't sit clearly on a solid deck, before it snaps back into an intact board at 3.5s.
